# Integration-test pcap fixtures

Small, license-clean pcaps for the end-to-end suite in `tests/integration/`.
All are generated by `make_fixtures.py` (pure `struct` packing, fixed
timestamps — no capture libraries, no randomness), so regeneration is
byte-for-byte reproducible; `tests/test_fixture_repro.py` pins this.

Regenerate:

    uv run python tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py

Not to be confused with `tests/data/`, which holds reader-level golden
samples (pcap + captured tshark output) owned by the reader unit tests.

## tcp_mixed.pcap

| # | Frame | Notes |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | TCP SYN `10.0.0.1:51234 → 10.0.0.2:443` | `tcp.port` dissects twice with different values: `(51234, 443)` — multi-value semantics |
| 2 | TCP SYN-ACK `10.0.0.2:443 → 10.0.0.1:51234` | reverse direction |
| 3 | TCP SYN `10.0.0.3:52000 → 10.0.0.2:8080` | second flow, disjoint ports |
| 4 | UDP/DNS query `10.0.0.1:53534 → 10.0.0.9:53` (`mixed.example` A) | `tcp.*` absent |
| 5 | ARP request who-has `10.0.0.2` tell `10.0.0.1` | `ip.*` and `tcp.*` absent — absent-field semantics |

## ctrl_comments.pcapng

Control characters in a string field value (issue #74). pcapng rather than
pcap because a frame *comment* is the one place a capture can carry arbitrary
bytes verbatim: every string field a dissector builds — `dns.qry.name`
included — is already `format_text`-ed by the dissector and can never hold a
raw control byte. All seven frames are the same TCP SYN; only
`frame.comment` differs.

| # | `frame.comment` | `-T fields` prints | Notes |
|---|-----------------|--------------------|-------|
| 1 | `tab<0x09>here` | `tab\there` | C-escaped |
| 2 | `vt<0x0b>here` | `vt\vhere` | 0x0b is also the reader's column separator, so this frame proves the separator cannot be forged by a value |
| 3 | `back<0x5c>slash` | `back\\slash` (>= 4.4) | the backslash doubling that makes the escaping invertible; 4.2.x prints `back\slash` |
| 4 | `us<0x1f>here` | `us<0x1f>here` | passed through RAW; 0x1f was the column separator before #74 and used to split the column and abort the parse |
| 5 | `C:<0x5c>temp` | `C:\\temp` (>= 4.4) | the collision that forces the version gate: 4.2.x prints `C:\temp`, byte-identical to what it prints for a value holding a real TAB, so unescaping there would rewrite this into `C:<0x09>emp` |
| 6 | (none) | (empty column) | `frame.comment` absent |
| 7 | `rs<0x1e>here` | `rs<0x1e>here` | passed through RAW like 0x1f, but 0x1e is the *occurrence* separator, so the fields path reports two occurrences (`("rs", "here")`) where `-T ek` reports the one true value. This is the residual #74 accepts rather than fixes — tshark returns `escape(occ1 + SEP + occ2)`, so no single-byte aggregator can recover the join positions. Appended after frame 6 so frames 1-6 keep the numbers the suite already pins |

## ntp_times.pcap

`FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME` renderings (issue #117). NTP's timestamps use the UTC
display base, which prints the zero ("not set") time as `NULL` in `-T fields`
and as the epoch in `-T ek`. The capture is dated 2023-11-05, so tshark before
4.6 prints a space-padded day in `-T fields` (`Nov  5, 2023 ...`).

| # | Frame | `ntp.reftime` | `ntp.org` | `ntp.rec` | `ntp.xmt` |
|---|-------|---------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | NTP client request `10.0.3.1:123 → 10.0.3.123:123` | zero | zero | zero | `00:00:05.5` |
| 2 | NTP server reply `10.0.3.123:123 → 10.0.3.1:123` | `2023-11-04 23:59:05` | `00:00:05.5` | `00:00:06.25` | `00:00:06.75` |

## guid_eui64.pcap

`FT_GUID` and `FT_EUI64` values (issue #69). tshark prints each the same way in
`-T fields` and `-T ek`, on 4.2.2 and 4.6.9.

| # | Frame | Field values |
|---|-------|--------------|
| 1 | DHCP DISCOVER, option 97 client UUID `00 11 22 .. ff` on the wire | `dhcp.client_id.uuid` = `33221100-5544-7766-8899-aabbccddeeff` (the dissector reads the first three groups little-endian) |
| 2 | SIP OPTIONS `10.0.4.1:5060 → 10.0.4.2:5060`, `Session-ID: AB30317F1a78...;remote=47755a9d...` | `sip.Session-ID.local_uuid` = `ab30317f-1a78-4dc4-8ff8-24d0d3715d86`, `.remote_uuid` = `47755a9d-e779-4ba3-8765-3f2099600ef2` |
| 3 | DNS response, one EUI64 (type 109) record | `dns.eui64` = `02:11:22:33:44:55:66:77` |
| 4 | ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation with a 16-byte SLLA option and an ARO | `icmpv6.opt.src_linkaddr_eui64` = `fe:00:00:00:00:00:a1:b2`, `icmpv6.opt.aro.eui64` = `02:11:22:33:44:55:66:77` |
| 5 | DHCP DISCOVER, client UUID `34 00 .. 00` on the wire | `dhcp.client_id.uuid` = `00000034-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`: below frame 1's by text order, above it by tshark 4.2.2's host-endian struct order |

## oid.pcap

`FT_OID` renderings (issue #149). Every frame is SNMP `10.0.5.1 → 10.0.5.2`.
tshark prints each OID as numeric dotted text, the same in `-T fields` and
`-T ek`, on 4.2.2, 4.4.19 and 4.6.9, except that `-T fields` cannot tell frame
11's lone empty value from absence. Frames 4 to 7 and 11 carry encodings no
conforming agent sends; frames 8 to 10 are well formed.

| # | Frame | Field values |
|---|-------|--------------|
| 1 | GetResponse, sysObjectID.0 and sysDescr.0 | `snmp.name` = `1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0`, `1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0`; `snmp.value.oid` = `1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.3.2.10` |
| 2 | SNMPv1 Trap | `snmp.enterprise` = `1.3.6.1.4.1.9` |
| 3 | GetResponse | `snmp.name` = `1.3.6.1.2.1.1.10`, `1.3.6.1.2.1.1.9`: arc order and text order disagree |
| 4 | GetResponse | `snmp.name` = `1.3`, `2.999.1`, then an arc of 2**32, which prints as the empty string and ends dissection (`[Malformed Packet]`) |
| 5 | GetResponse, name encoded `2b 06 81` (unterminated arc) | `snmp.name` = `1.3.6` |
| 6 | GetResponse, name encoded `2b 80 01` (non-minimal arc) | `snmp.name` = `1.3.1` |
| 7 | GetResponse, name with no content octets | `snmp.name` = `0` |
| 8 | GetResponse, name encoded `2b 06 ff 7f` | `snmp.name` = `1.3.6.16383` |
| 9 | GetResponse, name encoded `2b 06 81 80 00` | `snmp.name` = `1.3.6.16384`: one arc above frame 8, but tshark's byte order sorts it below |
| 10 | GetResponse, two varbinds | `snmp.name` = `1.3.6.1.2.1.0`, `1.3.6.1.2.1.3`: one on each side of the subtree `1.3.6.1.2.1.1`, none inside it |
| 11 | GetResponse, one varbind | `snmp.name` = an arc of 2**32 alone: prints as the empty string, which `-T ek` keeps and `-T fields` reads as absent |
